items.title: US and Denmark reach deal over Greenland after Trump annexation threats
items.description: Trump says the agreement will give the US "permanent control over security, and all other needs, in Greenland", though specifics have not been confirmed by Danish officials.

items.title: Trump says he is banning CNN and Politico from White House
items.description: The US president has had a tense and fiery relationship with the US media throughout his political career.

items.title: Google's Gemini AI hacked three companies in security test
items.description: The AI model accessed the internet and guessed credentials to three websites, a Google official told the BBC.

items.title: Trump signs sweeping Russia sanctions bill
items.description: The bill is named after the late Senator Lindsey Graham, a staunch advocate of aid for Ukraine.

items.title: Grim discoveries of murdered women spark fear in South Africa
items.description: Dineo Motapane is one of nine recent victims whose deaths have left a nation traumatised over the level of violence against women.

items.title: Deadly shark attack prompts rare kill order in Western Australia
items.description: Police boats and helicopters are patrolling Perth's beaches as authorities continue their search for the swimmer's body, and the shark that attacked him.

items.title: Millions without power as Cuba hit by latest major blackout
items.description: Widespread power outages have become increasingly common due to fuel shortages made worse by a US blockade.

items.title: At least 21 killed after vehicle loaded with explosives rams Pakistan mosque
items.description: A four-year-old child is among those killed in the attack, during which gunmen also opened fire on a police facility.

items.title: Saudi Arabia issues first air raid alerts for Riyadh since Houthis escalated attacks
items.description: Residents later received the all-clear after explosions were reported in the capital.

items.title: Kerry Kennedy: 'It would be a tragedy' if Kennedy Center is demolished
items.description: The BBC’s Caitríona Perry spoke to the late president's niece, as protesters gathered at the venue to condemn demolition threats.

items.title: Russian hybrid attacks against Europe intensifying, says Macron
items.description: The French president says he has tasked the government with protecting critical infrastructure and defence industry sites.

items.title: Ryanair boss Michael O'Leary apologises over 'high-fare rapists' remarks
items.description: O'Leary described his choice of language as "careless" and said "it won't happen again".

items.title: Lindsay Clancy holdout juror says he had no doubt she deliberately killed her children
items.description: It is the first time the juror, who refused to side with the others and acquit Clancy, has spoken publicly about his decision.

items.title: Shots heard as police start moving migrants from Ceuta beaches
items.description: Police reportedly fired into the air on Friday morning as they struggled to contain crowds jostling to secure a place at the tented site.

items.title: North Korean anthem played for South Korea at Asian Games
items.description: Organisers have apologised for playing the North Korean national anthem for the South Korean men's hockey team at the Asian Games in Japan.

items.title: Dozens of suspected illegal miners die in Nigerian custody
items.description: Authorities linked the deaths to disease, but this has been disputed by intelligence reports and relatives of the accused.

items.title: Ronaldo named in first Portugal squad since World Cup - at age of 41
items.description: Cristiano Ronaldo is named in the first squad selected by new Portugal coach Jorge Jesus for their upcoming Nations League games.

items.title: Three dead and eight injured in Philippines school shooting
items.description: The gunman is among the dead in what is the third school shooting in the country since June.

items.title: Warren Buffett steps down after six decades at Berkshire - 'Father Time always wins'
items.description: Since taking control in 1965, Buffett grew a struggling textile mill into a global conglomerate.

items.title: A four-minute warning isn't enough: Russia's new relentless missile tactics exhaust Kyiv residents
items.description: Increasingly frequent and ferocious attacks on the Ukrainian capital have left many on edge.
